status_reason: The design cannot be approved yet: the fiber type, link length and routing are not supplied, and the sources document no mid-IR fiber reach over 40 m, so the CIR link is blocked until AFS confirms it.
answer: Do not approve the 40 m all-CIR design yet. CIR fiber cuts off near 6.5 µm and no mid-IR link of 40 m is documented. Test MIR ATR at the melt first, using a PIR fiber as in the extrusion example, and compare it with NIR.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR at the melt with a diamond-cone probe and PIR fiber before approving the 40 m link
inline.probe: Diamond-cone ATR probe in the hot melt
inline.install: At the extruder melt stream (die area), as in the extrusion example
inline.fiber: PIR (polycrystalline), 3-17 µm, in place of the proposed CIR
inline.not_final_because: The 40 m MIR link is not documented, CIR cuts off near 6.5 µm, the additive band positions, polymer type and probe rating at 260 °C are unknown.

problems.text: The 40 m mid-IR link is not documented: the long 100-300 m cables are for low-OH silica (Vis-NIR), and the mid-IR comparisons are shown only for 2 m lengths.
Approval is requested before the facts needed for it are given: fiber type, link length, routing and conditions are missing, and method choice depends on them.
CIR fiber cuts off near 6.5 µm, so an all-CIR link cannot carry any band beyond that; the documented extrusion example used PIR fiber (3-17 µm).
The temperature rating of the probe and fiber at 260 °C is not stated; the extrusion example measured hot polymer with a diamond-cone ATR probe but gives no temperature figure.

methods.why: The extrusion example measured an API in hot polymer with a diamond-cone ATR probe via PIR fiber, and ATR fiber probes suit soft solids and liquids at a distance.
NIR runs on remote fiber probes, penetrates several millimetres and was used at the die of a hot-melt extruder, but needs chemometrics.
Raman is complementary to MIR, but its signal is weak and can be masked by fluorescence.
Most chemicals do not fluoresce, so it applies only if the additive does.

questions.q: What is the additive, and where are its mid-IR bands (cm-1 or µm)?
questions.why: If the bands lie above 6.5 µm, CIR cannot carry them and PIR is needed.

questions.q: What is the exact link length and routing from the melt to the control room, and can the FTIR sit closer?
questions.why: A 40 m mid-IR link is not documented, so the analyzer location decides feasibility.

questions.q: What polymer grade, filler type and additive concentration range are used?
questions.why: Fillers and concentration range set the validation design and whether ATR contact is reliable.

questions.q: What temperature and pressure rating does the probe need at 260 °C?
questions.why: No rating is given in the sources, and the probe must survive the melt.

experiment.objective: Check whether MIR ATR in the melt tracks additive concentration against independent laboratory values, and whether a mid-IR fiber link of the required length is feasible.
steps: Confirm additive identity, polymer grade, filler and concentration range with the client.
Record MIR ATR spectra of melt samples at known additive levels and identify the additive bands.
Pilot a diamond-cone ATR probe on an extruder die, coupled to an FTIR via PIR fiber, as in the extrusion example.
Measure the same samples with an NIR probe at the die and compare both on one held-out validation set with independent lab reference values.
Test the fiber over the planned link length and confirm transmission in the required range before any design approval.
references: S02 p.14 (extrusion ATR and NIR example)

pathway.key_features: Additive mid-IR band positions (not given) and whether they lie below 6.5 µm, which decides CIR versus PIR.
pathway.path_reason: Lab trials on the client's melt must come before key features and a model can be selected.

multispectral.why: NIR and MIR differ in absorption and penetration depth, and combined methods were reported to help in complex media; a NIR probe is already used at the extruder die.
multispectral.test: Compare the fused model with MIR ATR alone on the same held-out batches against independent lab values; drop the combination if it does not win.

assumptions: The additive has an identifiable mid-IR band, which has not been stated.
Fillers do not prevent good ATR contact with the melt, which has not been stated.
The 40 m figure is the physical route length of the cable.
The 260 °C melt is the only process condition that matters for the probe.
The FTIR would be in the control room as described.
